import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.62

by V. P. Shunkov

Is a (conjugacy, $p$-conjugacy) biprimitively finite group finite if it has a finite
maximal subgroup ($p$-subgroup)? There are affirmative answers for conjugacy
biprimitively finite $p$-groups and for $2$-conjugacy biprimitively finite groups
(V. P. Shunkov, *Algebra and Logic*, **9**, no. 4 (1970), 291–297; **11**, no. 4 (1972),
260–272; **12**, no. 5 (1973), 347–353), while the statement does not hold for arbitrary
periodic groups, see Archive, 3.9.

A group $G$ is *biprimitively finite* if for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$ any two
elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. It is *conjugacy
biprimitively finite* (a Shunkov group) if for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$ any two
conjugate elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup, and
*$p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite* if for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$ any two
conjugate elements of order $p$ in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. A *maximal
subgroup* is a maximal proper subgroup. Groups are not assumed to be periodic.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.62»

/-- A group $G$ is *biprimitively finite* if for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$ any two
elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsBiprimitivelyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group $G$ is *conjugacy biprimitively finite* (a *Shunkov group*) if for every finite
subgroup $H$ of $G$ any two conjugate elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite
subgroup. -/
def IsConjugatelyBiprimitivelyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime → IsConj x y → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group $G$ is *$p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite* if for every finite subgroup $H$ of $G$
any two conjugate elements of order $p$ in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsPConjugatelyBiprimitivelyFinite (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      orderOf x = p → orderOf y = p → IsConj x y → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- Every finite group is biprimitively finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBiprimitivelyFinite.of_finite [Finite G] : IsBiprimitivelyFinite G :=
  fun _ _ _ _ _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A biprimitively finite group is conjugacy biprimitively finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBiprimitivelyFinite.isConjugatelyBiprimitivelyFinite (h : IsBiprimitivelyFinite G) :
    IsConjugatelyBiprimitivelyFinite G :=
  fun H hH x y hx hy _ => h H hH x y hx hy

/-- A conjugacy biprimitively finite group is $p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite for every
prime $p$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsConjugatelyBiprimitivelyFinite.isPConjugatelyBiprimitivelyFinite
    (h : IsConjugatelyBiprimitivelyFinite G) {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) :
    IsPConjugatelyBiprimitivelyFinite p G :=
  fun H hH x y hx hy hxy => h H hH x y (hx ▸ hp) (hy ▸ hp) hxy

/-- A group is conjugacy biprimitively finite if and only if it is $p$-conjugacy biprimitively
finite for every prime $p$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isConjugatelyBiprimitivelyFinite_iff :
    IsConjugatelyBiprimitivelyFinite G ↔
      ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → IsPConjugatelyBiprimitivelyFinite p G :=
  ⟨fun h _ hp => h.isPConjugatelyBiprimitivelyFinite hp, fun h H hH x y hx _ hxy =>
    have ⟨_, hc⟩ := hxy
    h _ hx H hH x y rfl hc.orderOf_eq.symm hxy⟩

/--
Is a biprimitively finite group finite if it has a finite maximal subgroup?

This is the reading of the question with both parenthetical alternatives omitted.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsBiprimitivelyFinite G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

/--
Is a conjugacy biprimitively finite group finite if it has a finite maximal subgroup?

This is the reading of the question with the first parenthetical alternative "conjugacy".
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsConjugatelyBiprimitivelyFinite G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

/--
Is a $p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite group finite if it has a finite maximal subgroup
which is a $p$-group?

This is the reading of the question with the parenthetical alternatives "$p$-conjugacy" and
"$p$-subgroup", for every prime $p$. The maximal subgroup is a maximal proper subgroup of the
group that happens to be a finite $p$-group; it is not a maximal $p$-subgroup in the Sylow
sense.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPConjugatelyBiprimitivelyFinite p G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M ∧ IsPGroup p M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

/--
There is an affirmative answer for conjugacy biprimitively finite $p$-groups: for every
prime $p$, a conjugacy biprimitively finite $p$-group with a finite maximal subgroup is finite
(V. P. Shunkov, *Algebra and Logic*, **9**, no. 4 (1970), 291–297).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».variants.conjugacy_p_group : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPGroup p G →
      IsConjugatelyBiprimitivelyFinite G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

/--
There is an affirmative answer for $2$-conjugacy biprimitively finite groups: a $2$-conjugacy
biprimitively finite group with a finite maximal subgroup which is a $2$-group is finite
(V. P. Shunkov, *Algebra and Logic*, **11**, no. 4 (1972), 260–272; **12**, no. 5 (1973),
347–353). This is the case $p = 2$ of the $p$-conjugacy reading of the question.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».variants.two_conjugacy : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPConjugatelyBiprimitivelyFinite 2 G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M ∧ IsPGroup 2 M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

/--
The statement does not hold for arbitrary periodic groups (see Archive, 3.9): it is not true
that every periodic group with a finite maximal subgroup is finite. For example, in a Tarski
monster every non-trivial proper subgroup has prime order and is a finite maximal subgroup.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».variants.periodic :
    ¬ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Monoid.IsTorsion G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.62»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.62

by V. P. Shunkov

Is a (conjugacy, $p$-conjugacy) biprimitively finite group finite if it has a finite
maximal subgroup ($p$-subgroup)? There are affirmative answers for conjugacy biprimitively
finite $p$-groups and for $2$-conjugacy biprimitively finite groups (V. P. Shunkov,
*Algebra and Logic*, **9**, no. 4 (1970), 291–297; **11**, no. 4 (1972), 260–272;
**12**, no. 5 (1973), 347–353), while the statement does not hold for arbitrary periodic
groups, see Archive, 3.9.

A group $G$ is *biprimitively finite* if for every finite subgroup $H \le G$, any two
elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. It is *conjugacy
biprimitively finite* (a *Shunkov group*) if for every finite subgroup $H \le G$, any two
*conjugate* elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. For a prime
$p$, it is *$p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite* if for every finite subgroup $H \le G$, any
two conjugate elements of order $p$ in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup.

The question is read as three questions, one for each way of resolving the parentheticals:
"biprimitively finite" with "finite maximal subgroup", "conjugacy biprimitively finite" with
"finite maximal subgroup", and "$p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite" with "finite maximal
subgroup that is a $p$-subgroup". In the last reading the maximal subgroup is a maximal
subgroup of $G$ that happens to be a $p$-group, not a Sylow $p$-subgroup.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.62»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- The section $N_G(H)/H$ of a group $G$ at a subgroup $H$: the quotient of the normalizer
of $H$ by $H$. -/
abbrev normalizerQuotient (H : Subgroup G) : Type _ :=
  H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer

/-- A group $G$ is *biprimitively finite* if for every finite subgroup $H \le G$, any two
elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsBiprimitivelyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ x y : normalizerQuotient H, (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime →
      Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group $G$ is *conjugacy biprimitively finite* (a *Shunkov group*) if for every finite
subgroup $H \le G$, any two conjugate elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite
subgroup. -/
def IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ x y : normalizerQuotient H, (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime → IsConj x y →
      Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group $G$ is *$p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite* if for every finite subgroup
$H \le G$, any two conjugate elements of order $p$ in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite
subgroup. -/
def IsPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ x y : normalizerQuotient H, orderOf x = p → orderOf y = p → IsConj x y →
      Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A biprimitively finite group is conjugacy biprimitively finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBiprimitivelyFinite.isConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (hG : IsBiprimitivelyFinite G) :
    IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G :=
  fun H hH x y hx hy _ => hG H hH x y hx hy

/-- For a prime $p$, a conjugacy biprimitively finite group is $p$-conjugacy biprimitively
finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite.isPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite
    (hG : IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G) {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) :
    IsPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite p G :=
  fun H hH x y hx hy hxy => hG H hH x y (hx ▸ hp) (hy ▸ hp) hxy

/-- A finite group is biprimitively finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBiprimitivelyFinite.of_finite [Finite G] : IsBiprimitivelyFinite G :=
  fun _ _ _ _ _ _ => inferInstance

Is a biprimitively finite group finite if it has a finite maximal subgroup?

Here a maximal subgroup of $G$ is a maximal proper subgroup, i.e. a coatom of the lattice
of subgroups of $G$.
-/

theorem kourovka.«6.62».parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsBiprimitivelyFinite G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M) → Finite G := by

maximal subgroup which is a $p$-subgroup? The statement is quantified over all primes $p$.

The maximal subgroup is a maximal proper subgroup of $G$ that is a $p$-group; it is not a
Sylow $p$-subgroup (a maximal element among the $p$-subgroups).
-/

      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M ∧ IsPGroup p M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

/--
For every prime $p$, a conjugacy biprimitively finite $p$-group is finite if it has a finite
maximal subgroup. This is the affirmative answer for conjugacy biprimitively finite $p$-groups
(V. P. Shunkov, *Algebra and Logic*, **9**, no. 4 (1970), 291–297).
-/

    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPGroup p G →
      IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

A $2$-conjugacy biprimitively finite group is finite if it has a finite maximal subgroup
which is a $2$-subgroup. This is the affirmative answer for $2$-conjugacy biprimitively finite
groups, i.e. the case $p = 2$ of the $p$-conjugacy reading of the question
(V. P. Shunkov, *Algebra and Logic*, **11**, no. 4 (1972), 260–272; **12**, no. 5 (1973),
347–353).
-/

    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite 2 G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M ∧ IsPGroup 2 M) → Finite G := by

monster every non-trivial proper subgroup has prime order, so it is a finite maximal

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.62

by V. P. Shunkov

Is a biprimitively finite group, or one of its conjugacy variants, finite if it
has a finite maximal subgroup? The notebook also records two affirmative
special cases and notes that the corresponding claim for arbitrary periodic
groups is false.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46),
problem 6.62.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.62»

/-- A group is biprimitively finite if, for every finite subgroup $H$, any two
elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsBiprimitivelyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Subgroup G), Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group is conjugacy biprimitively finite (a Shunkov group) if, for every
finite subgroup $H$, any two conjugate elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$
generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Subgroup G), Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      IsConj x y → (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime →
        Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group is $p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite if, for every finite subgroup
$H$, any two conjugate elements of order $p$ in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite
subgroup. -/
def IsPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Subgroup G), Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      IsConj x y → orderOf x = p → orderOf y = p →
        Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/--
Is every biprimitively finite group with a finite maximal proper subgroup
finite?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsBiprimitivelyFinite G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

/--
Is every conjugacy biprimitively finite group with a finite maximal proper
subgroup finite? No periodicity assumption is imposed on the group.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

/--
For every prime $p$, is every $p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite group with a
finite maximal proper subgroup which is a $p$-group finite? Here "maximal"
means maximal among all proper subgroups, not maximal among $p$-subgroups.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      IsPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite p G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M ∧ IsPGroup p M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

/--
The conjugacy biprimitively finite $p$-group case has an affirmative answer:
for every prime $p$, such a group with a finite maximal proper subgroup is
finite.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».variants.conjugacy_p_group : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G → IsPGroup p G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

/--
The $2$-conjugacy case has an affirmative answer: every $2$-conjugacy
biprimitively finite group with a finite maximal proper subgroup which is a
$2$-group is finite.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».variants.two_conjugacy : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite 2 G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M ∧ IsPGroup 2 M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

/--
The analogous assertion for arbitrary periodic groups is false: there exists
an infinite periodic group with a finite maximal proper subgroup.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».variants.periodic : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Monoid.IsTorsion G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.62»
